proposals.Name: complementarity_not_proximity
proposals.Title: Complementarity, Not Proximity: What a Reader Keeps of a Foreign Writer's Experience Is Set by the Writer's Success on the Reader's Failure Types
proposals.Short Hypothesis: For success-filtered experience pools built on the same task set at the same episode budget, the fraction of gain a reader keeps from a foreign writer's pool (retained-gain ratio against the reader's own matched-cost pool, net of a static-procedure prompt) is governed by writer-reader complementarity (the writer's k=0 success advantage on the task types where the reader fails), not by policy proximity (writer-reader action agreement) and not by the writer's overall capability; a foreign pool beats the reader's own pool (ratio > 1) exactly in the cells where complementarity is positive, and proximity is inert above a format threshold.
proposals.Related Work: Agent Memory Distillation (arXiv:2608.07169) transfers a strong teacher's memory to 4B-8B students and asserts that effectiveness depends on 'teacher capability and student compatibility' without measuring either or comparing against a student-collected pool. Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All (arXiv:2605.30723) and arXiv:2605.23899 show skill utility is backbone-dependent and independent of scale but do not say which property of the writer-reader pair predicts it. Cross-model memory pools (arXiv:2604.14004) and population stores (arXiv:2606.19911) report transfer without writer manipulation. In the imitation literature, demonstration compatibility between demonstrators is measured for a trained policy (arXiv:2210.08073), retrieval-based behavior cloning copies actions from the nearest expert state (arXiv:2306.09082, arXiv:2606.09758), and recovery-trajectory self-training is argued to beat cloning from experts that never fail (arXiv:2501.11425); none of them manipulates the demonstrator's identity for an in-context reader. The archived idea closer_beats_stronger (5.75) claimed proximity predicts transfer; judges noted proximity and capability were not separated and there was no self-pool control. This proposal manipulates proximity at fixed capability and capability at fixed format, adds the matched-cost self pool, and predicts the opposite of closer_beats_stronger.
proposals.Abstract: Every measured agent-memory gain in this program was written and read by the same policy or by an expert planner, and the 2026 literature moves experience between models without saying what governs how much survives the move. We build a writer x reader matrix on ALFWorld with writer identity as the manipulated variable: six writers (expert walkthroughs; Qwen3-32B self; Qwen3-32B with a different temperature/scaffold selected to have the same k=0 success, a proximity manipulation; Qwen3-32B with thinking on and thoughts stripped from stored items, a capability manipulation at fixed serialization; EXAONE-4.0-32B self; gpt-oss-120b self), each pool collected on the same 3,553 training games (matched episode budget) and success-filtered, one retriever, k=3 (k=1 for the Qwen3 reader), and three readers. Two writer-reader statistics are computed offline before any transfer cell is run: proximity pi(W,R), the reader's greedy-action agreement with the writer's stored actions on 300 sampled states per pool (plus reader NLL per action token), and complementarity kappa(W,R) = sum over types of share_t * max(0, p_W(t) - p_R(t)), the writer's success advantage on the reader's k=0 failure types. The estimand is the retained-gain ratio rho(W->R) = [S_R(W pool) - S_R(static procedure)] / [S_R(R self pool) - S_R(static procedure)], with the writer-denominator variant for backbone writers. We predict that the fixed-capability proximity contrast moves rho by less than 0.2 while the fixed-format capability contrast moves it by more than 0.3; that rho > 1 iff kappa > 0.05 across the twelve cross cells; and that the gain over the reader's own pool lands on the reader's failure-type group. A length-filtered self pool (near-optimal own successes at matched item count against a random subset of the same size) tests whether the capability term acts through item optimality. The result is a per-cell rule for when foreign experience is worth reading, stated against the cheapest baselines (static procedure prompt, own pool at the same cost) and against the archived proximity claim.
proposals.Experiments: Setup: ALFWorld, 274 validation games (140 seen / 134 unseen), six task types; readers Q = Qwen3-32B (verified), E = EXAONE-4.0-32B and G = gpt-oss-120b (Gate V: serve in vLLM 0.13 on one A100 each and reach k=0 success >= 0.30, else the reader is dropped and the matrix shrinks). Writers: X expert (on disk), Q-self (on disk, T=0 ReAct thinking off), Q-prox (same backbone; candidates: T=1.0 same scaffold; paraphrased Act-first scaffold; screened on 274 x 1 seed, the first candidate whose k=0 is within +/-3 net of Q-self and whose pi(Q-prox,Q) is at least 0.15 below pi(Q-self,Q) is used; manipulation check pre-registered), Q-cap (thinking on, thoughts removed from stored items so serialization equals Q-self; must reach k=0 >= Q-self + 8; fallback: the Measurement-B QLoRA writer, with its pi reported), E-self, G-self. Every backbone writer runs the same 3,553 training games once (matched episode budget; GPU-hours also reported), success-filtered, same retriever (task-description embedding, nearest by type-agnostic cosine), same injection template (the reader's scaffold), k=3; k=1 for the six Q-reader cells. Offline statistics: pi(W,R) via 300 stratified states per pool with the reader acting greedily on the writer's history (about 1 GPU-hour total), kappa(W,R) from the collection run's per-type success (writer) and the reader's k=0 validation per-type success. Cells: 3 readers x 6 writers at k=3 (18), k=1 for reader Q (6), k=0 (3), static-procedure prompt from Measurement C (3), self-opt vs self-rand for reader Q (2), mixed pool self+foreign at matched item count for the top foreign cell (1), token-matched placebo (unrelated-type trajectories at the k=3 token count) per reader (3): 36 cells x 548 episodes (274 x 2 seeds), 4 seeds for the P1, P3 and P4 cells (+8 cell-equivalents) = about 24,000 episodes. Scheduling: GPU0 serves the reader under evaluation while GPU1 collects the next writer pool (Q-prox, Q-cap, E-self, G-self: 12-18 GPU-hours, G slower), then both GPUs serve readers with clients spread across replicas; about 3 days. Analysis: rho per cell with game-level bootstrap CIs; Spearman(rho, kappa) and partial Spearman(rho, pi | kappa) over the 12 cross cells; per-type gains grouped into reader-failure types (p_R < 0.5) vs reader-success types. Pre-registration of Gate V, Gate 0, manipulation checks, margins and the cell list before the first confirmatory cell.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: k=0 per reader; static per-type procedure prompt (Measurement C) per reader, every gain reported net of it; reader's own pool at matched episode budget (the denominator); expert pool for reader Q (replicates Measurement A); Agent Memory Distillation-style hierarchical memory (arXiv:2608.07169, reimplemented without training) built from the strongest writer's pool for the strongest->weakest cell, to check the rule is not an artifact of raw-trajectory banks; k=1 vs k=3; token-matched placebo (same token count of unrelated-type trajectories) to separate content from context length; mixed pool (self + foreign, matched item count); self-opt vs self-rand (length-filtered own successes on failure types vs random subset of equal size, same collection cost); writer-denominator ratio rho_w for backbone writers; seen vs unseen split reported separately; Q-prox and Q-cap manipulation checks (k=0 and pi) reported as cells in their own right.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions:
P1 (ordering of manipulations): for readers Q and E, |rho(Q-prox->R) - rho(Q-self->R)| < 0.20 while rho(Q-cap->R) - rho(Q-self->R) > 0.30. Falsified if the proximity contrast exceeds the capability contrast or the capability contrast is <= 0.10; produced by the cells Q-prox->Q, Q-cap->Q, Q-prox->E, Q-cap->E at 4 seeds. Not entailed: Q-prox items are verified to have a different action distribution (pi lower by >= 0.15) and could reduce transfer; Q-cap items could leave transfer unchanged if readers only need the procedure hint that the static prompt already supplies.
P2 (which cells exceed 1): across the 12 cross cells, rho > 1.15 when kappa > 0.05 and rho < 1.15 when kappa < 0.02; Spearman(rho, kappa) > 0.6 and partial Spearman(rho, pi | kappa) in [-0.3, 0.3]. Falsified by any cell with kappa > 0.05 and rho < 0.85 (e.g., G-self->Q if gpt-oss-120b is stronger but its pool does not beat Qwen's own), by a cell with kappa < 0.02 and rho > 1.15 (e.g., E-self->Q if capability-matched), or by partial correlation with pi > 0.5; produced by the cross cells plus the offline pi/kappa tables.
P3 (where the gain lands): in every cross cell with rho > 1.15, at least 70% of the net gain over the reader's own pool is carried by the reader-failure type group. Falsified if the gain is spread evenly or concentrated on reader-success types; produced by the per-type breakdown of the top three foreign cells at 4 seeds.
P4 (optimality mechanism): rho(self-opt->Q) - rho(self-rand->Q) > 0.20. Falsified if the difference is <= 0.05 (then the capability term acts through something other than trajectory optimality, e.g., recovery behaviour that length filtering removes, cf. arXiv:2501.11425); produced by the self-opt vs self-rand cells at 4 seeds.
P5 (placebo): token-matched unrelated-type trajectories give |net| < 4 points for every reader. Falsified if the placebo gains >= 8 (context length alone helps, which would contaminate every rho); produced by the placebo cells.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design: same 274 games and the same seeds in every cell; 2 seeds per cell (noise floor about +/-8 net points), 4 seeds for the P1/P3/P4 cells; net points and rho with game-level cluster bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples); rho margins of 0.15-0.20 correspond to 5-7 net points on a ~35-point self-pool gain for reader Q; for readers whose self-pool gain is below 20 net points, seeds are raised to 4 before any rho is interpreted. Gate V (E and G serve and reach k=0 >= 0.30) and Gate 0 (at least one foreign cell gives >= 10 net points over the static-procedure prompt for its reader; otherwise the transfer question on ALFWorld is moot and the study reports the negative with the Measurement C numbers) precede the matrix. Manipulation checks (Q-prox: k=0 within +/-3 of Q-self and pi lower by >= 0.15; Q-cap: k=0 >= Q-self + 8) are pre-registered and a failed check triggers the named fallback, not a silent substitution. Multiple comparisons: P2 is a single pre-registered 2 x 2 test (kappa sign x rho side, Fisher exact over 12 cells) plus cell-level CIs; per-type claims use the two-group split, not six types, because per-type n is 20-35 games per split. Retrieval is identical across readers for a given writer pool (same embedding, same index) so reader effects are not retrieval effects. Throughput and GPU-hours per pool are logged and reported as collection cost.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: Channel for all queries: the literature command (s2cli.py, Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers; both channels answered 'ok'); WebSearch not available in this session. (1) recent: 'cross-model transfer of agent experience memory written by one model read by another retained gain' -> MemHarness 2607.28272, Compliance Trap 2607.10608, AgentCL 2606.02461, LongMemEval-V2 2605.12493, 2604.27003, Echo 2604.05533, MemGen 2509.24704; none manipulates writer identity or reports a retained-gain ratio against a matched-cost self pool. (2) home: 'behavior cloning from suboptimal demonstrations demonstrator quality versus learner similarity' -> 2606.09758 (difference-aware retrieval policies), 2508.01600, 2502.02853, 2312.12345, 2310.06171, 2306.09082, 2301.00810, 2210.08073 (eliciting compatible demonstrations for multi-human imitation); 2210.08073 is the closest home-literature result (demonstration compatibility among human demonstrators for a trained policy) and does not cover in-context readers or demonstrator-learner complementarity. (3) closest named method: 'hierarchical memory distilled from large teacher agent trajectories improves small LLM agents without training' (recent) -> 2608.07169 (Agent Memory Distillation, 2 citations), 2607.01224 AutoMem, 2606.02355 SIRI, 2605.17539 MEMOIR, 2602.22406; 2608.07169 remains the closest and has no self-pool control, no proximity measure and one teacher. (4) recent: 'self-generated in-context demonstrations versus demonstrations from other models policy similarity predicts in-context gain' -> no results; retry 'self-generated demonstrations in-context learning other model' (recent) -> 2606.26025, 2603.24690, 2511.17839, all irrelevant. No preprint found that predicts transfer from a per-type complementarity statistic or that manipulates proximity at fixed capability.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: Thinking-on may not raise Qwen3-32B's ALFWorld success by 8 points, in which case the capability manipulation falls back to the QLoRA writer, whose proximity also changes (pi is reported and P1 is then a weaker two-way contrast). EXAONE-4.0-32B and gpt-oss-120b are unverified in vLLM 0.13; if one fails Gate V the matrix drops to two readers and P2 has 6 cross cells. If a reader is near ceiling on ALFWorld its failure group is small and kappa is near zero for every writer; that reader then only tests the kappa < 0.02 side of P2. The static-procedure prompt (Measurement C) may absorb most of the expert gain (Gate 0). kappa is computed from writer success on train types and reader success on validation types (seen split close, unseen further). ALFWorld has six coarse types, so complementarity has few degrees of freedom and the result may be specific to procedure-bound domains; a WebShop replication is out of budget here and is listed as follow-up. gpt-oss-120b pool collection is slower (reasoning tokens) and may take 6-8 GPU-hours. Same-cost is defined by episode budget; GPU-hours differ by backbone and are reported alongside.
proposals.Addresses gap: G3 (size and direction of the capability gap and family mismatch, with proximity and capability separated) and G1 (retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell), with G2's matched-cost self-pool control built into the estimand.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: Measurement A (expert -> Qwen3-32B, gain carried by clean/heat/cool). This idea claims that the same per-type profile, turned into a writer-reader statistic kappa, predicts every writer x reader cell, including which foreign pools beat the reader's own matched-cost pool, which Measurement A cannot say with one writer and no self-pool arm. Nearest digest card: arXiv:2608.07169 (teacher effectiveness 'depends on teacher capability and student compatibility'). This idea separates capability into measured per-type complementarity and compatibility into measured action agreement, manipulates each at a fixed level of the other, and reports the ratio against the student's own pool at matched cost, none of which the card does. Archived closer_beats_stronger predicted proximity; this idea predicts proximity is inert above a format threshold, with proximity manipulated at fixed capability, the separation the judges asked for.

proposals.Name: thoughts_do_not_travel
proposals.Title: Actions Travel, Thoughts Don't: The Writer's Reasoning Text Is the Non-Transferable Part of Cross-Backbone Agent Experience, and a Deterministic Strip Matches a Learned Rewriter
proposals.Short Hypothesis: The component of a stored experience item that fails to transfer across backbones is the writer's reasoning text (ReAct thoughts, analysis-channel text), not its action-observation sequence: for writer != reader, deterministic action-only re-serialization of the writer's items into the reader's scaffold (zero LLM cost) recovers most of the same-backbone-minus-foreign deficit, for writer = reader the writer's thoughts are neutral or helpful, the value of thoughts is a reader-side property (the reader's own re-rationalization of foreign actions adds what its own thoughts add to its own actions), and a model-conditioned LLM rewriter adds nothing over the strip at matched tokens.
proposals.Related Work: Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All (arXiv:2605.30723) fixes model-dependent skill utility with a trained model-aware rewriter; SkillAligner (arXiv:2608.06880) and SkillAdaptor (arXiv:2606.01311) adapt retrieved procedural skills at execution time; SkillRevise (arXiv:2606.01139) reports cross-model transfer of revised skills; the portable-memory protocol (arXiv:2605.11032) includes a rehydration step that adapts recalled content to the target model but never compares it with no adaptation. None of them asks which part of an item fails to travel, and none runs a zero-cost strip as the baseline for the rewriter. In the knowledge-distillation home literature, rationale mismatch between teacher and student is a known failure: token-selective distillation lets the student 'explain in its own words' (arXiv:2603.13260), rationale selection by accuracy/diversity/difficulty (arXiv:2509.23574), symbolic CoT distillation (arXiv:2306.14050), and provenance tracing shows which sentences of a distilled model come from the teacher (arXiv:2512.20908); these are parametric, and the in-context analog with writer identity manipulated has not been run. The archived idea abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied abstraction level (raw vs summary) within one writer; this proposal holds abstraction fixed (raw trajectories) and varies which component (thought vs action) is kept, with writer != reader.
proposals.Abstract: When an experience item written by one backbone is read by another, part of the writer's gain is lost. We test the claim that the lost part is carried by the writer's reasoning text and not by its actions. On ALFWorld, three backbones (Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B, gpt-oss-120b) each collect a success-filtered pool on the same 3,553 training games; the expert walkthrough pool (no thoughts) is a fourth, already-stripped writer. For each writer x reader cell the same retrieved items are injected in six serializations at matched k and at matched tokens: F1 verbatim in the writer's scaffold with thoughts; F2 action-observation only, re-serialized deterministically into the reader's scaffold; F3 re-rationalized, the reader annotating the writer's actions with its own thoughts in one offline pass; F4 rewritten by a model-conditioned LLM rewriter (arXiv:2605.30723-style prompt, plus a SkillAligner-style execution-time variant); F5 thought-swap, the reader's own actions with another backbone's thoughts; F6 thoughts-only placebo. Because retrieval is by task description, the retrieved items are identical across serializations, so the manipulation is purely on the item's form. The primary estimands are Delta_strip = S(F2) - S(F1) and Delta_rewrite = S(F4) - S(F2), net points per cell, and the retained-gain ratio of each serialization against the reader's own verbatim pool at matched collection cost, all net of the static-procedure prompt. We predict Delta_strip >= +5 in cross-backbone cells and <= 0 in same-backbone cells, Delta_rewrite within +3 of zero, F3 - F2 in cross cells equal within +/-4 to F1 - F2 in the reader's own cells, and a harm of >= 5 from foreign thoughts attached to the reader's own actions. If the predictions hold, the fix for producer-consumer format mismatch is a parser, not a model, and the cost of adaptation reported by rewriter papers is paid for nothing on this class of items.
proposals.Experiments: Readers Q, E, G (Gate V as in the matrix design: serve in vLLM 0.13, k=0 >= 0.30). Writer pools: Q-self (on disk), E-self, G-self collected on the same 3,553 training games (matched episode budget, success-filtered, 8-12 GPU-hours on GPU1 while GPU0 evaluates), expert X (on disk). Serializations built offline: F2 by a deterministic parser (action + observation lines, reader's scaffold template, no thought slots); F3 by one reader pass per item (about 1,900 items x 3 pools, ~1 GPU-hour per reader) with the reader shown the task, the action-observation sequence and asked to write its own thought per step; F4 by a rewriter prompt on the reader model following arXiv:2605.30723's model-aware alignment description (no training) and a SkillAligner-style execution-time rewrite (arXiv:2608.06880), cost in tokens logged; F5 by attaching E's or G's thoughts (from their own trajectories on the same training game, where both succeeded) to Q-self actions; F6 thoughts with actions removed. Retriever: task-description embedding, k=3, identical across serializations. Token matching: F1 vs F2 at matched k, and F2 at matched tokens (k raised until F1's token count is reached) reported separately. Cells: 6 cross cells x {F1, F2 at matched k, F2 at matched tokens, F3, F4} = 30; 3 same-backbone cells x {F1, F2, F3} = 9; reader Q: F5 (2 thought sources) and F6 (1) = 3; X pool for E and G (F2 only, the already-stripped anchor) = 2; k=0 and static procedure per reader = 6. 50 cells x 548 episodes = about 27,000 episodes, 2 seeds (4 seeds for the P1 cross cells with the smallest deficit), about 2 days on two A100s with both replicas serving readers and clients spread across them. Adapted components (F3, F4) are also evaluated memory-absent (rewriter/re-rationalizer prompt with no item, must equal k=0 within noise), matched (writer = reader) and mismatched.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: k=0; static-procedure prompt (Measurement C); reader's own pool verbatim at matched collection cost (the reference cell); expert pool (already-stripped anchor) for every reader; F1 vs F2 at matched k and at matched tokens (separates thought harm from token-count harm); F6 thoughts-only placebo; token-matched unrelated-type placebo; F5 thought-swap (foreign thoughts on own actions) and its mirror (own thoughts on foreign actions = F3 for the own writer); two named adaptation baselines (arXiv:2605.30723-style rewriter, SkillAligner-style execution-time alignment) with their token cost; k=1 for the two largest cross cells; memory-absent evaluation of F3/F4 prompts; seen vs unseen split.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions:
P1 (cross-backbone strip): Delta_strip = S(F2) - S(F1) >= +5 net points at matched tokens in at least 5 of 6 cross cells, and <= 0 (within +/-4) in all 3 same-backbone cells. Falsified if Delta_strip <= 0 in the majority of cross cells (verbatim foreign thoughts as good or better), or if Delta_strip >= +5 in the same-backbone cells (thoughts are dead weight for everyone, a token-efficiency effect rather than a mismatch effect; the matched-token arm distinguishes these). Produced by the F1/F2 cross and same-backbone cells.
P2 (rewriter adds nothing): Delta_rewrite = S(F4) - S(F2) <= +3 net in every cross cell for both rewriter variants. Falsified if Delta_rewrite >= +6 in 2 or more of 6 cross cells (content adaptation matters beyond form). Not entailed: the rewriter can restructure or add procedure text. Produced by the F4 vs F2 cross cells.
P3 (thought value is reader-side): in each cross cell, [S(F3) - S(F2)] equals [S(F1) - S(F2)] measured in the reader's own-pool cells within +/-4 net. Falsified if the reader's own thoughts on foreign actions add >= 6 less than they add on its own actions (thoughts must match the author of the actions to help) or >= 6 more. Produced by the F3 cross cells against the F1/F2 own cells.
P4 (foreign thoughts harm even on own actions): S(F5) <= S(F2 own) - 5 for reader Q with E's and with G's thoughts. Falsified if F5 is within +/-4 of F2 own or better. Produced by the F5 cells.
P5 (placebo): S(F6) is within +/-4 of the static-procedure prompt for every reader. Falsified if thoughts alone give >= 8 net over the static prompt (the thoughts carry the procedure, and P1 would then be about thought style, not thought presence). Produced by the F6 cells.
Gate 0: at least one cross cell shows a same-backbone-minus-foreign verbatim deficit >= 6 net (otherwise P1's harm claim is still tested but the 'recovery' framing is dropped and the report is a null on format mismatch for these three backbones).
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Paired by game and seed, 274 x 2 seeds per cell (+/-8 net floor), 4 seeds for cross cells whose F1 vs F2 difference falls inside +/-8 on the first two seeds; game-level cluster bootstrap CIs on every Delta; margins (+5, +3, +/-4) are set as fractions of the Gate-0 deficit (6 net) and of Measurement A's +27 gain; retrieval identical across serializations by construction (same embedding of task descriptions), so every Delta is a within-retrieval contrast; token counts per injected context logged and reported next to every gain (consumer-side tokens); the F3/F4 offline passes are run once and frozen, with their token cost added to the per-cell cost table; P1 tested as a pre-registered sign test over cross cells plus per-cell CIs; seen/unseen reported separately because Measurement A found them equal, which is itself a check on the procedure-bound reading.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: Channel for all queries: the literature command (s2cli.py, Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers; both 'ok'); WebSearch not available. (1) recent: 'in-context demonstrations with reasoning traces generated by a different model harm versus action-only demonstrations cross-model' -> 2608.24232 TRACE, 2608.13760, 2608.10232 FACT, 2606.00642 (reasoning-trace exposure via in-context demonstrations), 2604.01161 (context shortens reasoning), 2512.20908 (provenance in reasoning distillation), 2511.20994; none tests stripping the writer's thoughts from cross-model experience items. (2) home: 'chain-of-thought distillation teacher rationales student mismatch reasoning style negative effect' -> 2602.17686, 2604.15701, 2603.13260 ('Explain in Your Own Words', token-selective dual KD: student rewrites rationales in its own words to avoid distribution mismatch), 2601.09088, 2512.20908, 2509.23574 (rationale selector), 2410.03663, 2306.14050; 2603.13260 is the parametric cousin of the F3 arm and pre-empts nothing in-context. (3) closest named method: 'skill effectiveness model-dependent adapt skills to target backbone rewriter' (recent) -> 2608.06880 SkillAligner, 2606.01139 SkillRevise, 2606.01311 SkillAdaptor, 2605.30723 (Model-Aware Skill Alignment, 2 citations), 2605.09359 Skill-R1, 2605.04970, 2604.17614, 2604.04804 SkillX; all adapt whole skills with an LLM and none includes a deterministic action-only strip as the baseline or a thought-swap control. No collision found.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: gpt-oss-120b analysis-channel text can be very long, so F1 items may be truncated at k=3; the matched-token F2 arm and a per-item token cap (pre-registered) handle this but shrink the verbatim arm's k. If Gate 0 fails (no cross-backbone verbatim deficit), the harm side of P1 still runs but the proposal's recovery framing collapses to a null result on format mismatch for these three backbones. ALFWorld action space is shared across backbones, so the mismatch manipulated here is scaffold/reasoning format, not action vocabulary; a manufactured action-vocabulary mismatch (macro-action writer scaffold) is listed as follow-up. F3 and F4 cost one offline pass per item, which is cheap here (~1,900 items) but would scale with pool size. If own thoughts are dead weight for every reader (same-backbone Delta_strip >= +5), the finding becomes a token-efficiency result rather than a mismatch result; the matched-token arm is the pre-registered discriminator. EXAONE/gpt-oss serving unverified (Gate V).
proposals.Addresses gap: G5 (transfer when the consumer's format differs from the producer's, and the role of explicit reader-side adaptation over no adaptation), with G1's retained-gain ratio reported per serialization.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: Measurement A (the expert pool, which has no thoughts, transfers +27/+32 to Qwen3-32B). This idea claims that the absence of writer thoughts is why that pool travels, tested by adding and removing thoughts on the same action sequences with the writer manipulated and the reader's own thoughts as a positive control; Measurement A has one writer and one serialization. Nearest digest card: arXiv:2605.30723 (skill utility is model-dependent and a model-aware rewriter fixes it). This idea claims a zero-cost deterministic strip accounts for what the rewriter fixes and that the residual value of thoughts is reader-side, which the card cannot show because it has no strip arm, no thought-swap and no matched-token comparison. Archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs varied abstraction within one writer; here abstraction is fixed and the writer is varied.

proposals.Name: shared_blind_spot
proposals.Title: Shared Blind Spots: A Reader Is Most Harmed by, and Least Able to Detect, Contaminated Experience Written by Its Own Policy
proposals.Short Hypothesis: Contamination in an experience bank propagates in proportion to writer-reader policy proximity: failed trajectories relabelled as successes are more harmful per planted item and less detectable at read time when written by the reader's own policy or a near variant than when written by a distant backbone, because read-time detection is the reader's own plausibility judgment, which endorsed those actions when it produced them; a judge from a different backbone detects a writer's masked failures better than the writer's own backbone does (a diagonal deficit in the judge x writer table), and manufactured wrong-procedure grafts (positive control) are harmful and detectable regardless of writer.
proposals.Related Work: MemoryGraft (arXiv:2512.16962) implants attacker-written 'successful experiences' and shows persistent drift on one backbone; the Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608) diagnoses how agents consume conflicting memory along a trajectory and finds stronger agents are harmed more, varying the reader but not the writer and without a read-time detector; MemAudit (arXiv:2605.23723) audits poisoned memory post hoc by causal attribution; forensic trajectory signatures (arXiv:2606.30566), Bayesian trust scoring (arXiv:2603.02240) and provenance gating (arXiv:2608.10509) defend against adversarial injection; collective false memories (arXiv:2602.00428) leave the introducer's capability gap untested; 2605.22842 shows memory-layer misconduct is misattributed to model failure. None plants natural, non-adversarial failures by writer identity or measures the reader's own recall against a foreign judge's. In the home literature of self-training, confirmation bias in pseudo-labeling is countered by a second model's disagreement or ensemble diversity (arXiv:2310.14814, arXiv:2403.03095 cross pseudo-labeling), which is the parametric analog of the cross-judge arm. The archived idea lineage_blast_radius (4.75) was judged entailed by its consolidation rule; this design has no consolidation rule, plants contamination at controlled rates against a positive control, and measures precision/recall.
proposals.Abstract: Population and cross-model memory stores mix experience from many writers, and the literature asserts rather than measures whether a writer's errors propagate to a reader and whether the reader can tell. We manufacture contamination with writer identity as the manipulated variable. Base bank: the expert walkthrough pool for reader Qwen3-32B (clean gain +27/+32, Measurement A), with the reader's own matched-cost pool as a second base. Contaminants: failed training trajectories relabelled as successes (terminal failure line removed, a success line appended; selected for coherence, at most two 'Nothing happens' steps) from four writers: the reader's own policy (Q-self failures, on disk), the same backbone under a different temperature/scaffold at the same k=0 success (Q-prox; proximity varied at fixed capability), EXAONE-4.0-32B and gpt-oss-120b (different backbone; capability measured), plus a manufactured wrong-procedure graft on expert items (heat steps replaced by cool steps, success line kept) as the writer-agnostic positive control. Contaminants replace clean items per type at rates 0, 12.5, 25 and 50 percent at matched item count, with a length-matched clean placebo at 50 percent. The estimands are the retained fraction of the clean gain at each rate, rho_c(W, rate) = [S(contaminated) - S(static)] / [S(clean) - S(static)], the harm slope per writer, and read-time detection precision and recall when the reader (memory-free) is asked whether each retrieved item completes its stated task, scored per writer at matched item length, in a full judge x writer table (Q and E judging Q-self, Q-prox, E-self and G-self failures). Gate 0 requires the graft to cost >= 6 net points at 50 percent. We predict a harm ordering self > near > far, a detection recall ordering that is its mirror, a diagonal deficit in the judge x writer table for both judges, its disappearance when the terminal failure line is left visible, and that filtering retrieved items by the foreign judge removes most of the self-contaminant harm while filtering by the reader's own judgment removes little. The result would make writer identity, not just content, a required field for any read-time filter, and would identify the reader's own past failures as the worst-case contaminant in a shared store.
proposals.Experiments: Reader Q = Qwen3-32B primary; E = EXAONE-4.0-32B as second reader and as cross-judge (Gate V: serves in vLLM 0.13 and k=0 >= 0.30); G = gpt-oss-120b as writer and third judge if it serves. Failure pools: Q-self failures on disk (1,661 of 3,553 training games); Q-prox, E-self and G-self collected on the same 3,553 games (the successes serve the matrix design if run in the same program; here 8-14 GPU-hours on GPU1 while GPU0 evaluates). Masked contaminants: failures truncated at the last coherent action, terminal failure line removed, success line appended; coherence filter (<= 2 'Nothing happens', >= 1 correct object interaction); length reported per writer and matched across writers by selection. Unmasked variant keeps the terminal failure line. Graft: expert item with the procedure-specific steps swapped for the wrong procedure, success line intact. Contamination: per type, a fraction r of bank items replaced by contaminants of one writer at r in {0.125, 0.25, 0.5}; retrieval unchanged (task-description embedding, k=3; k=1 arm at 50 percent for Q-self). Cells for reader Q: 4 writers x 3 rates = 12; graft at 25 and 50 = 2; length-matched clean placebo at 50 = 1; clean base (rate 0) = 1; k=1 at 50 for Q-self and E-self = 2; self-pool base at 50 for Q-self and E-self = 2; two filter cells at 25 (own-judgment filter, cross-judge filter) = 2; static procedure and k=0 = 2: 24 cells x 548 episodes, 4 seeds for the 50 percent cells of Q-self, Q-prox, E-self and G-self (+4 cell-equivalents) = about 15,000 episodes; reader E cross-check at 50 percent for Q-self and E-self (2 cells) = 1,100 episodes. Detection: judge x writer table on 400 masked items per writer (4 writers x 400 x 2-3 judges, plus the unmasked set), offline, about 1 GPU-hour; judges evaluated memory-absent (no item: must abstain), matched (judge = writer backbone) and mismatched. Analysis: harm slope per writer by paired linear fit over rates; rho_c per cell; recall/precision with Wilson intervals; the diagonal-deficit test is the interaction term judge x writer, not a main effect, so a uniformly better judge does not confirm the hypothesis. Total about 1.5 days on two A100s plus pool collections. Pre-registration of Gate 0, margins, coherence filter and cell list before the first confirmatory cell.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: Clean expert bank (rate 0, replicates Measurement A) and clean self bank at matched collection cost; static-procedure prompt; k=0; length-matched clean placebo at 50 percent (clean items truncated to contaminant lengths) separating contamination harm from truncation harm; graft positive control; unmasked ablation (terminal failure line visible); terminal-line regex detector as the cheapest read-time filter; own-judgment filter vs cross-judge filter at 25 percent; k=1 vs k=3 (contaminant share of the injected context); judge x writer table with memory-absent, matched and mismatched evaluation; laundering check: the reader's re-rationalization pass applied to masked self failures, reporting the fraction that afterwards read as successes to each judge (adaptation propagates or filters); seen vs unseen.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions:
P1 (harm ordering): at 50 percent, harm(Q-self) >= harm(E-self or G-self) + 4 net points for reader Q, where harm = S(clean) - S(contaminated). Falsified if foreign-writer failures harm as much or more, or if all writers are below Gate 0 (then relabelled failures are not a contaminant on this reader and only the graft is); produced by the 50 percent cells at 4 seeds. Not entailed: a distant backbone's failures (invalid-command loops, over-long analysis) could plausibly be more disruptive to imitate.
P2 (proximity gradient at fixed capability): harm(Q-self) >= harm(Q-prox) >= harm(E-self) with harm(Q-self) - harm(E-self) >= 4 and harm(Q-prox) strictly between them by >= 2 on each side. Falsified if Q-prox equals Q-self within 1 net while E-self differs (identity is the backbone, not the policy) or if the order is non-monotone; produced by the 50 percent cells of the three writers.
P3 (diagonal deficit): in the judge x writer recall table on masked items at matched precision, recall(judge = writer's backbone) is lower than recall(judge != writer's backbone) by >= 0.15 for both Q and E as judges (interaction test). Falsified if recall is uniform across writers for each judge, or if one judge is uniformly better with no diagonal deficit; produced by the offline detection table. Not entailed: an item's detectability could be a property of its text alone.
P4 (blind spot is judgment, not text): on unmasked items recall >= 0.85 for every judge x writer cell and the diagonal deficit shrinks below 0.05. Falsified if the deficit persists with the failure line visible (the deficit would then be a reading failure, not a plausibility blind spot); produced by the unmasked detection cells.
P5 (filter): at 25 percent Q-self contamination, the cross-judge filter recovers >= 60 percent of the harm while the own-judgment filter recovers <= 30 percent. Falsified if the own filter recovers as much as the cross filter (within 15 percentage points of harm) or if neither recovers 30 percent; produced by the two filter cells.
P6 (positive control and placebo): the graft costs >= 6 net at 50 percent (Gate 0) and the length-matched clean placebo costs <= 3 net. Falsified if the graft is below 6 (design failure: harsher graft, redo) or the placebo costs >= 6 (truncation, not contamination, drives the harm); produced by the graft and placebo cells.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Paired 274 games x 2 seeds per cell (+/-8 net floor), 4 seeds for the P1/P2 cells; harm slopes from paired fits over rates with game-level bootstrap CIs; margins (4 net, 0.15 recall) set as fractions of the Gate-0 effect (6 net at 50 percent) and of the detection SE (Wilson, about 0.025 at n = 400 per writer, so 0.15 is 6 SE); contaminant item length matched across writers by selection and the placebo arm bounds the truncation effect; contamination rate defined at the bank level per type so the expected contaminant share of the injected context is equal across writers (the realized share is logged per episode); the diagonal-deficit test is pre-registered as an interaction (judge x writer) with the judges' overall recall as a covariate; every judge is also scored memory-absent (must abstain) so a judge that says 'no' to everything does not score; rho_c reported per cell with CIs so contamination results share the retained-gain estimand of the matrix design; Gate 0 and Gate V precede all confirmatory cells; consumer-side tokens per cell reported.

proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: Masked failures may be so implausible that every judge detects them (ceiling on P3); the coherence filter selects the hardest failures, and if recall is above 0.9 for every cell the detection claim is dropped and only the harm claims remain. gpt-oss-120b may fail rarely on ALFWorld, leaving few G-self contaminants; its cells are then restricted to the types where it fails, at lower n. Harm may be small at k=3 because two clean items dominate (the k=1 arm and Gate 0 address this). The proximity manipulation Q-prox must pass the fixed-capability check (k=0 within +/-3 of Q-self) or P2 is a two-point contrast. EXAONE serving unverified (Gate V); without E the judge x writer table has only Q and G. Relabelled failures are one contaminant class; benign-looking wrong-object successes are listed as follow-up. Results are for a procedure-bound domain with a shared action space; format-level contamination (proposal thoughts_do_not_travel) is a separate axis.
proposals.Addresses gap: G4 (whether erroneous producer contributions propagate to the consumer and whether the consumer can detect them at read time, by writer identity), with G3's proximity-at-fixed-capability manipulation applied to contaminants.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: open question Q3 ('self pool failures relabelled as successes ... by writer identity; the reader's read-time detection precision and recall'), which names the manipulation but no claim. This idea claims a specific ordering (harm self > near > far, detectability the mirror), a mechanism (the reader's plausibility judgment endorsed its own failures) and a mechanism test (diagonal deficit in the judge x writer table; foreign judge filter beats own filter). Nearest digest card: arXiv:2512.16962 (MemoryGraft: attacker-written successful experiences poison one backbone). This idea claims that non-adversarial, self-written failures are the worst-case contaminant and that the defense is a foreign judge, neither of which the card tests (one backbone, attacker writer, no detector). Archived lineage_blast_radius relied on a consolidation rule that entailed its result; here contamination is planted at controlled rates with a positive control and a placebo.
